subject: Concord Bank MAP: SOC 2 / CAIQ / DPA timeline and data-archiving notes
messages:
From: Alex Mercer <alex.mercer@concordbank.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
Cc: Concord Bank Legal <contracts@concordbank.com>
Date: Fri, 01 Oct 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: MAP & security lane — Concord Bank evaluation

Hi Marissa / Rafael,

Thanks for the demo yesterday — Concord's evaluation committee liked the throughput numbers and the routing/fallback examples. We're ready to land the MAP but need clarity on the security gating items before we commit to the production cutover date. High level asks from legal and platform:

- SOC 2: We need the latest SOC 2 Type II report and a 1-page control summary that maps controls to your hosted / private variants.
- CAIQ/SIG: A filled CAIQ or SIG-lite snapshot is required for our vendor intake team.
- DPA: Concord legal will propose a few redlines we need to negotiate; retention windows and deletion triggers are the primary sticking points.
- Data retention / archive: Concord has a 7-year archival policy for PII tied to specific product buckets; we need confirmation of retention granularity (customer-level vs. token-level) and export/escrow options.

We attached a draft MAP and a short timeline suggestion. Target close for contract signature is 2027-11-12; security acceptance needs to be complete 3 weeks prior for internal board signoff. Can you confirm what dates you can commit to for each gate? Also, any standard escrow or long-term archive workflow you support (S3 escrow + key escrow / HSM) would be useful to note.

Attachments: MAP_v1_ConcordBank.xlsx (map + milestones)

Best,
Alex Mercer
Head of Platform Risk — Concord Bank

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Mercer <alex.mercer@concordbank.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 01 Oct 2027 11:26:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP & security lane — Concord Bank evaluation

Alex — thanks, great to hear the demo landed with the committee. I've pulled Rafael and Kim on this thread so we can align on concrete dates and artifacts. Summary of our initial position below and proposed schedule: 

1) SOC 2: We can provide the latest SOC 2 Type II and a one-page control mapping for hosted and private lanes. Rafael will attach a SOC2-Control-Summary.pdf by EOD Monday.
2) CAIQ: We maintain a CAIQ-lite snapshot and will populate the sections Concord requested; target delivery: 2027-10-06.
3) DPA redlines: We reviewed Concord's standard list; we generally accept most operational-level clarifications but retain standard liability and data-processing scope carveouts. We're attaching a proposed redline set (DPA-proposed-redlines.docx). Rafael, can you call out any non-starters?
4) Data retention & archive: We support retention at the customer-namespace level (per-customer buckets) and token-level TTLs for ephemeral caches. Long-term archival (7+ years) is supported via configurable S3 export to a customer-owned bucket with optional key-escrow; we will include a short technical appendix describing the export + key-handover flow.

Proposed MAP cadence (we can tighten):
- 2027-10-04: SOC2 control summary + CAIQ-lite draft (deliverables)
- 2027-10-11: Legal redlines + internal call to review DPA changes
- 2027-10-18: Final security acceptance checklist and evidence intake (SOC 2 + CAIQ + DPA signoff)
- 2027-11-12: Contract signature (target)

I attached a fresh MAP (MAP_v2_ConcordBank.xlsx) with the above dates. If Concord needs an escrow/archival playbook, we can propose a simple S3-based escrow plus a DPA addendum that notes responsibility for long-term key custody. Rafael / Kim — please add any engineering or legal caveats below.

Attachments: MAP_v2_ConcordBank.xlsx

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Director, Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference

From: Alex Mercer <alex.mercer@concordbank.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>, Concord Bank Legal <contracts@concordbank.com>
Date: Mon, 04 Oct 2027 08:09:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP & security lane — Concord Bank evaluation

Marissa — appreciate the clear plan and quick turnaround. A couple clarifications from legal and compliance after a quick read-through: 

- Retention granularity: Concord legal prefers retention tied to account IDs (customer-level) rather than wider namespaces; is that straightforward?
- Export cadence: we'd prefer an automated monthly export to our archive bucket with a manifest and an integrity checksum.
- Escrow: Concord legal is comfortable with S3 export but requests that the export package be encrypted with customer-managed keys (CMK) and that Redwood provide a signed attestation of the export process.

On DPA redlines: legal will send a first-pass Word file (separate email) — we expect ~5 targeted changes around deletion triggers and subprocessors. If Redwood can agree to an escrow export cadence and the attestation, that will resolve most concerns.

Thanks — can we hop on a 30-minute call tomorrow at 10am PT to walk through the escrow/attestation flow?

— Alex

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
To: Alex Mercer <alex.mercer@concordbank.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Concord Bank Legal <contracts@concordbank.com>
Date: Mon, 04 Oct 2027 16:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP & security lane — Concord Bank evaluation

Alex / Concord Legal team — Rafael here (security & compliance engineering). Quick technical notes to confirm we can meet the ask and to surface a couple of caveats before tomorrow's call: 

- Retention granularity: We can implement retention tied to Concord account ID. That means each account's persisted objects are tagged by account_id and exported per-month to a Concord-owned S3 bucket. We will not co-mingle customer archives.
- Export cadence: We can automate a monthly export (cron-managed job) with a manifest that includes file checksums (SHA256) and a signed manifest by our CI system. Exports can be encrypted using Concord-provided KMS CMKs — Redwood supports cross-account KMS encrypt-to-key workflows.
- Attestation: We can provide an export attestation (signed PDF) that describes snapshot integrity and the encryption process. Standard attestation will be included as part of the MAP evidence package; for highly-regulated flows we can provide additional HSM-backed signing on request (may need a 2-3 week lead).
- DPA redlines: We reviewed the doc Marissa attached. Kimberly (legal) — the only items likely to require executive signoff are: 1) change to deletion trigger language (we propose a 30-day window post-request for deletion of live data, with longer archival retention by default), and 2) subprocessors clause where Concord requests prior notice vs. prior consent.

Action items: 
- Rafael to upload SOC2-Control-Summary.pdf and CAIQ-lite draft to the HubSpot record by 2027-10-04 EOD.
- Concord to send DPA redlines; Redwood will produce a marked-up Word by 2027-10-11.
- Schedule: Confirm tomorrow's 10am PT call (DocuSign invite or calendar hold) — Marissa to send.

Attachments referenced: SOC2-Control-Summary.pdf, DPA-proposed-redlines.docx

Cheers,
Rafael Mendes
Senior Security Engineer — Redwood Inference
